item.title: Approved Website Assets Need a Manifest
item.description: Before using approved website images in a redesign, collect them into a clean asset archive with folders, hashes, friendly filenames, and a rename map.

item.title: Page Images Need a System, Not a Search Spree
item.description: Website images should be chosen, mapped, and maintained like content. A simple image system keeps pages from feeling generic, repetitive, or disconnected.

item.title: Dropdown Navigation Needs Structure and Feedback
item.description: A dropdown menu is not just a place to hide links. It needs clear grouping, readable spacing, and current-state feedback so users know where they are and where they can go next.

item.title: Static Site Migrations Need a URL Contract Before a Redesign
item.description: A static-site migration should start with a complete URL contract. Before redesigning anything, preserve every page, feed, image, sitemap, and hidden route so the new build does not quietly break the old site.

item.title: Your Static Site Build Should Not Rewrite Every Page
item.description: A static site build that rewrites every page creates noisy deployments. Here's why deterministic output matters and how to keep generated files under control.

item.title: The Website Link Is Not the GitHub Repo
item.description: A private GitHub repository, a local preview, and a public website URL are three different things. Keeping those links straight prevents launch confusion.

item.title: Removing Outdated Website Claims Takes More Than One Search
item.description: When a website needs outdated claims removed, do not only edit the visible paragraph. Search components, metadata, generated pages, and built output before calling it done.

item.title: The Website Rebuild Step That Saves the Whole Project
item.description: Before rebuilding a business website, inventory the current pages, images, content, and conversion paths. It prevents redesigns from losing useful assets and search value.

item.title: The Typo That Silently Breaks Your Static Site (And How to Catch It)
item.description: A wrong frontmatter key in your static site generator won't throw an error — it will just silently do nothing. Here's the story of a missing blog image and what it teaches about debugging config-driven systems.
